title: Comparative structural analysis of protein complexes with SPICE.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the full GitHub repository tree (51 non-cache entries) and the Zenodo deposit via its application programming interface (API). Everything shipped is Python source code, compiled caches, nine example notebooks, and exactly two Protein Data Bank (PDB) coordinate files: examples/data/5GGS_wt.pdb (342 kB) and examples/data/212__5GGS__H_100_Y_H.pdb (342 kB). Zenodo record 18509536 holds one file, PyPDBcomplex.zip, 4.0 MB, licence CC-BY-4.0. The web server https://spice.cs.ucr.edu returns HTTP 200. There is no measurement table, no feature/label file, and no benchmark set anywhere in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The geometric thresholds used by the tool (hydrogen bond donor-acceptor within 3.5 angstrom, salt bridge within 4.0 angstrom, disulfide sulfur-sulfur 2.0-2.2 angstrom, 1.4 angstrom solvent probe), the claim that run time drops from minutes to seconds, and the feature-comparison table against PDBePISA, PISA, MAPIYA, PIC and PRODIGY. I did not submit a job to the web server.

a1_downloadable.note: The software downloads freely: Zenodo DOI resolves to record 18509536 (PyPDBcomplex.zip, 4.0 MB, CC-BY-4.0) and the GitHub repository is public, no login. What downloads is code, not data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Nothing in the deposit contains a prediction target. The only plausible labels for this data type - measured binding affinity or change in binding free energy on mutation - appear in no file here; they would have to be imported wholesale from SKEMPI 2.0 or PDBbind, i.e. constructed from outside sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Structures are present as actual coordinates rather than accession numbers, but only two of them (5GGS wild type and one H-chain position-100 Tyr mutant); the tool otherwise fetches structures from RCSB on demand.

a4_units_stated.note: No data table exists to carry units. The paper also states the van der Waals energies are 'relative rather than absolute binding energies', so the tool's main energetic output has no stated physical unit.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Two PDB files shipped as case-study examples. Checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 4 MB zip; 0.68 MB of PDB coordinates
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; running the descriptors over a large PDB set would also be CPU-only, but there is no set shipped.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper claims no dataset counts at all, and the two case studies (1A2Y, 5GGS) match the two shipped structures, so there is nothing to disagree about.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL. There is no measured label. Every quantity the tool emits (buried surface area, bond counts, van der Waals energy) is computed deterministically from the same atomic coordinates that would be the features, so using any of them as a target is leakage by construction, not biology.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) or ProteinMPNN-style structure encoders would fit the data type
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for embedding a few thousand interface sequences, but there is nothing here to train a head on
backbone.licence: Software is CC-BY-4.0 on Zenodo; the article itself is CC-BY-NC-4.0

integration.partner_dataset: SKEMPI 2.0 (345 wild-type complexes, ~7,085 measured mutants) or PDBbind, joined on PDB identifier plus chain and residue position
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do cheap geometric interface descriptors add anything to a protein language model when predicting measured binding free energy changes - a question answerable entirely from SKEMPI plus RCSB, with this paper contributing only a convenience script.

controls.positive_control: None available in this deposit; with SKEMPI one would check that known hot-spot alanine substitutions come out destabilising.
controls.negative_control: Not runnable here - no labels to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: None in the paper; would have to come entirely from SKEMPI/PDBbind/AB-Bind.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from this paper's data: it ships a structural-analysis library and two example PDB files, so any model built 'from it' would in fact be a model trained on SKEMPI or PDBbind with SPICE used only as a feature calculator.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use geometric descriptors of a protein-protein contact surface to predict how strongly the two proteins stick together.
plain_idea.train_on: What the model would see: per-interface descriptors this tool computes from 3D coordinates - buried surface area, counts of hydrogen bonds, salt bridges and disulfide bonds, packing energy terms. Number of examples available from this paper: 2.
plain_idea.predict: Measured binding strength, or its change when one residue is mutated, normally measured by surface plasmon resonance or isothermal titration calorimetry. Those measurements exist only in external databases such as SKEMPI 2.0, not in this deposit.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Antibody and protein engineers would use a good interface-to-affinity predictor to triage mutants before making them; but this paper supplies only the descriptor calculator, so the project would belong to SKEMPI, not to this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: Two PDB files versus SKEMPI 2.0's ~7,085 measured mutants across 345 complexes, which the existing predictors already train on. There is no data advantage of any kind here.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements and in fact no measurements at all are shipped, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated from this deposit.

models_beatable.why: DDMut-PPI (2024, graph neural network), USP-ddG (2025, mixture-of-experts) and BindPred (2026, protein-language-model embeddings, reported Pearson r 0.89 on SKEMPI 2.0) are all recent and actively published; we would bring no new data to the contest.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model would see strictly less than the baselines, because this paper adds no measurements - only a re-implementation of descriptors (buried surface area, hydrogen bonds) that PPI-Affinity and PRODIGY already use as inputs.

ml_idea: The only project this paper could seed is 'use SPICE/PyPDBcomplex interface descriptors as features to predict measured binding affinity or affinity change on mutation', with labels taken from SKEMPI 2.0 and structures from RCSB. That is a SKEMPI project with a convenience feature-extractor bolted on, in a field already served by DDMut-PPI, USP-ddG, PPI-Affinity and BindPred; this paper contributes no data to it.

effort.compute_note: Sizes read directly from the GitHub tree and Zenodo API (4.0 MB zip, 0.68 MB of coordinates); no timing done because there is no dataset to time anything on.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the repository tree - one API call shows two PDB files and zero measurement tables, which kills it immediately.

verdict_reason: Pure web-tool paper. The deposit is a Python structural-analysis library plus two example PDB structures, with no measured label and no rows: Part A fails at A2, A5 and A8. Every quantity the tool emits is computed from the same coordinates that would be the features, so nothing here can serve as a prediction target; any real project would be a SKEMPI 2.0 project in an already crowded field.
